name: Enslaved
why: The 1994 debut is cold, long-form Viking black metal — no clean vocals, no prog polish, just frost and repetition. It's a completely different band from the one that plays festivals now, which is the whole point of the set.
pedigree: Grutle Kjellson and Ivar Bjørnson started this as teenagers; early drummer Trym left for Emperor.
usFrequency: Tours the US every couple of years, but almost never plays this material.
v3Note: Paige put this on her want-to-see list. My 9 was too high.

name: Candlemass
why: Enormous slow riffs under an operatic voice — closer to Blind Guardian's sense of drama than to anything else on this bill. If Paige only sees one legacy band, this is the one with actual tunes.
pedigree: Leif Edling's band; Epicus Doomicus Metallicus literally named the genre. Messiah Marcolin sings it in a monk's robe.
usFrequency: Rarely. US appearances come maybe once a decade.
v3Note: Paige put this on her want-to-see list. My 8 was too high.

name: Overkill
paigeNote: Classic thrash. Melodic for thrash, but thrash is the idiom the Exumer signal rejects outright.
why: East coast thrash with a singer who actually sings, and this set skips everything after 1991. Feel Elektrik and Deadly Sins territory.
pedigree: Bobby 'Blitz' Ellsworth and D.D. Verni have been there since 1980 — no reunions, no hiatus, 20-plus albums.
usFrequency: Constantly. Easiest band here to catch again.
specialSet: Old school set, first five albums

name: Autopsy
paigeNote: Deliberately filthy old-school death metal. No melodic payload.
why: Filthy, lurching, half-speed death metal that basically invented the death-doom template. More groove than most of the grind here, but no melody to hang onto.
pedigree: Chris Reifert drummed on Death's Scream Bloody Gore at 17, then quit to do this.
usFrequency: Very selective — festival sets only, no real touring.

name: Insect Warfare
paigeNote: Grindcore. Pure brutality.
why: Twenty minutes of the most worshipped American grind record of the 2000s. Historically a big deal, musically a blur.
pedigree: Houston band that made one album and split in 2009. Reunions only.
usFrequency: Almost never. This is the draw for the grind crowd.

name: Repulsion
paigeNote: Proto-grind. Pure brutality.
why: Horrified (1986) is one of the two or three records grindcore came from. Everything fast and gross on this bill traces back here.
pedigree: Scott Carlson and Matt Olivo; Carlson later played in Death and Cathedral.
usFrequency: Rare festival appearances only.

name: Voivod
paigeNote: Dissonant progressive sci-fi thrash — two negatives at once, thrash idiom plus dissonance.
why: Sci-fi thrash that sounds like nobody else — jagged, jazzy, strange. The deep cuts set means Killing Technology and Dimension Hatröss era.
pedigree: Away's artwork and Piggy's dissonant chords; Jason Newsted played bass with them after Metallica.
usFrequency: Tours North America regularly.

name: The Kovenant
why: Nexus Polaris (1998) is the missing link between Dimmu's Enthrone Darkness Triumphant and full space-opera symphonic black metal. If Paige scores one band a 10 before hearing a note, it's this.
pedigree: The big one: Nagash played bass in Dimmu Borgir; guitarist Astennu was in Dimmu too; Hellhammer of Mayhem drummed the album; Sarah Jezebel Deva (Cradle of Filth, Therion) sang on it.
usFrequency: Effectively never. They stopped playing this material decades ago.
v3Note: Paige put this on her want-to-see list with two stars. My 10 was too high.

name: Lucifer
why: Seventies-styled riff rock with a strong clean-sung hook on every song. The most relaxing forty minutes of the weekend, and genuinely well written.
pedigree: Johanna Sadonis (ex-The Oath) with Nicke Andersson of Entombed and the Hellacopters on drums.
usFrequency: Comes over occasionally, usually club tours.

name: Demolition Hammer
paigeNote: Brutal precision thrash with no melodic or atmospheric payload.
why: Brutally precise late-era thrash — all wrist and no chorus. Great to stand in front of, hard to hum.
pedigree: New York band; Epidemic of Violence is a cult record for the riff-obsessed.
usFrequency: Rare. Reunited relatively recently after a long absence.
v3Note: Paige put this on her maybe list. My 3 was too low.

name: YOB
paigeNote: Atmospheric doom with cleans, but glacial, hookless, and no Scandinavian cold. Emotional cleans also risk the whiny veto.
why: Slow, enormous and surprisingly melodic — Scheidt's clean wail carries whole songs. If Paige has patience for twelve-minute tracks there's real melody here.
pedigree: Mike Scheidt's band out of Eugene, Oregon.
usFrequency: Tours the US regularly.

name: Sabbat
paigeNote: Raw lo-fi blackened thrash; the King Diamond-ish theatrics don't offset thrash plus rawness.
why: Venom and Bathory filtered through Japanese eccentricity — theatrical, catchy, played in capes. Fun in a way most of this bill isn't.
pedigree: Gezol's band, running continuously since 1983 with a huge cult discography.
usFrequency: Extremely rare. A trip to the US is an event.
v3Note: Paige put this on her pass list. My 4 was too high.

name: Akercocke
paigeNote: Technical progressive death/black with chaotic gear changes. The Martyr lesson applies despite the atmosphere.
why: Satanic prog in Savile Row suits — clean vocals, jazz breaks and blastbeats in the same song. Choronzon (2003) is where the ambition and the aggression balance best.
pedigree: Jason Mendonça's band; the offshoot Voices came out of it.
usFrequency: Almost never leave Britain. This is close to a once-ever chance.
paigeQuote: death metal infused with electronic too many sound effects and random laughing in songs for me
v3Note: Paige put this on her pass list. My 4 was too high. Her words: “death metal infused with electronic too many sound effects and random laughing in songs for me.”

name: Naglfar
why: Ice-cold tremolo melody with real songwriting underneath. If In Flames and Dimmu Borgir are the poles of Paige's taste, Naglfar sits exactly between them.
pedigree: From the same mid-90s Swedish scene as Dissection and Dark Funeral; Kristoffer Olivius has fronted it for most of its life.
usFrequency: Very rare. They barely leave Europe.

name: Anaal Nathrakh
why: Chaos with sudden soaring clean choruses bolted on — the melodic moments are genuinely good, but you have to wade through a lot of noise to reach them.
pedigree: Mick Kenney and Dave Hunt, who also sang in Benediction.
usFrequency: Rare US appearances.
v3Note: Paige put this on her want-to-see list with two stars. My 4 was too low.

name: Left to Die
paigeNote: Early-Death material — brutal and non-melodic.
why: A tribute set by people with the right to play it. Historically satisfying rather than musically surprising.
pedigree: Rick Rozz and Terry Butler, both actual ex-Death members, playing the album they helped make possible.
usFrequency: Plays occasional anniversary shows.
v3Note: Paige put this on her pass list. My 4 was too high.

name: Exumer
paigeNote: Teutonic thrash. Confirmed not interested — this is the calibration point.
why: Second-tier German thrash in the best sense — Sodom energy with better riffs than its reputation suggests.
pedigree: Possessed by Fire is a Teutonic thrash staple; early member Ray Mensh crossed paths with the Kreator circle.
usFrequency: Rare US shows.

name: Onslaught
paigeNote: UK thrash — same idiom veto as Exumer.
why: British thrash with big shouted choruses. Sits somewhere near early Sepultura and Onslaught's own punk roots.
pedigree: Started as a hardcore punk band; The Force is the classic. Sy Keeler on vocals.
usFrequency: Very rare on this side of the Atlantic.

name: Vreid
why: Rocking, melodic Norwegian black metal with folk melodies buried in it — a straight line from Windir's Sognametal. Big, singable riffs.
pedigree: Formed by the surviving members of Windir after Valfar died in 2004.
usFrequency: Very rare in the US.

name: Saturnus
why: Mournful, melodic, guitar-lead-driven doom. This is the Wolfheart-adjacent slot on the bill and probably the biggest sleeper for Paige.
pedigree: Denmark's answer to early Anathema and Paradise Lost.
usFrequency: Essentially never come to the US.
v3Note: Paige put this on her want-to-see list. My 8 was too high.

name: Black Breath
paigeNote: Raw HM-2 crust death — heavy for heavy's sake.
why: Entombed's buzzsaw guitar plus hardcore drive. Short songs, real hooks, no pretension.
pedigree: Seattle band from the Southern Lord stable, back after a long break.
usFrequency: Active again and touring.
v3Note: Paige put this on her pass list. My 4 was too high.

name: Mortem
paigeNote: Lineage over sound. The Slow Death material is raw, not melodic — Euronymous oversaw it, Hellhammer drummed it, Dead did the cover, and the core became Arcturus. Confirmed excited.
why: The Slow Death EP (1989) is early Norwegian death metal before the scene turned black. Worth it for the genealogy alone.
pedigree: The deep-lore pick: this became Arcturus. Steinar Sverd Johnsen and Hellhammer of Mayhem both came through it.
usFrequency: Never, as far as I can tell.

name: Exhumed
paigeNote: Goregrind and death metal — brutality first.
why: Carcass worship done with real craft and a sense of humour. Gore Metal is the rawest thing they made.
pedigree: Matt Harvey's long-running Bay Area band; a revolving door of West Coast death metal players.
usFrequency: Tours constantly — you can always catch them again.

name: Sadistic Intent
why: Thirty-eight years in and still no debut album. Pure old-school evil, and a genuine curiosity for the death metal faithful.
pedigree: The Cortez brothers from LA; they've backed Possessed's Jeff Becerra live.
usFrequency: Rare — a few festival sets a year, no real tours.
v3Note: Paige put this on her pass list. My 4 was too high.

name: Panopticon
why: Long, melodic, genuinely moving — Kentucky and Roads to the North are the entry points. Closest thing on the bill to atmospheric melodic black metal with a heart.
pedigree: Austin Lunn plays nearly everything himself, and folds banjo and fiddle into black metal without it being a gimmick.
usFrequency: Barely plays live at all, which makes this notable.
v3Note: Paige put this on her pass list. My 8 was too high.

name: Benighted
paigeNote: Brutal death and grind.
why: Technically ferocious and very tight. Almost entirely rhythm, almost no melody.
pedigree: Julien Truchan's band; a fixture of the European brutal death circuit.
usFrequency: Comes over occasionally.

name: Thulcandra
why: Unapologetic Dissection worship: Storm of the Light's Bane melodies with modern production. If Paige likes Naglfar she'll like this, and vice versa.
pedigree: Fronted by Steffen Kummerer, who also leads Obscura — two of his bands on the same bill.
usFrequency: Rare US appearances.

name: Azarath
paigeNote: Blast-driven brutal blackened death; speed and force rather than melody.
why: Fast, Polish, precise, and darker than Behemoth's arena version of the same idea.
pedigree: Inferno, Behemoth's drummer, plays in this — it's his other band.
usFrequency: Rare.
v3Note: Paige put this on her want-to-see list with two stars. My 3 was too low.

name: Disharmonic Orchestra
paigeNote: Grind and experimental death; the chaos veto.
why: Grindcore that keeps wandering off into jazz chords and odd time. Weird in an interesting way rather than a punishing one.
pedigree: Early Nuclear Blast signing; part of the strange first wave of European grind.
usFrequency: Effectively never come to the US.

name: Gorerotted
paigeNote: Goregrind.
why: Gross-out British goregrind with a comedic streak and better riffs than the song titles suggest.
pedigree: Members went on to form The Rotted after the split.
usFrequency: Rare — they reunited relatively recently.

name: Martyr
paigeNote: Technical progressive death. Confirmed not interested — the second calibration point.
why: Quebec tech death from before tech death became a sport: fluid, jazzy, actually composed. Fans of the musicianship side of Children of Bodom will find something here.
pedigree: Daniel Mongrain plays guitar here and is now also in Voivod, who are on this same bill.
usFrequency: Rare — sporadic reunion shows.

name: Secret Chiefs 3
paigeNote: Cinematic but avant-garde; not her metal idiom.
why: The wild card of the weekend — surf guitar, Persian scales, film-score bombast. The Holy Vehm material is the darkest, heaviest corner of his catalogue.
pedigree: Trey Spruance of Mr. Bungle, who also wrote much of Faith No More's King for a Day.
usFrequency: Tours occasionally.
paigeQuote: whoa the falafel song is nuts

name: Funebrarum
why: New Jersey band doing early-90s Swedish death metal with total conviction. Warm, murky, riff-first.
pedigree: Daryl Kahan, also of Disma and ex-Winter.
usFrequency: Plays East Coast shows and fests, not much beyond.
v3Note: Paige put this on her maybe list. My 3 was too low.

name: Lamp of Murmuur
why: Raw black metal that keeps drifting into eighties goth and post-punk. If Night of the Vampire is a hit at home, this is the same neighbourhood with more menace.
pedigree: Started as a solo LA project, now a live band; one of the most talked-about names in the current raw black underground.
usFrequency: Plays rarely, and the shows sell out.

name: Guineapig
why: Pitch-shifted vocals, horror samples, no melody by design. Strictly for the grind constituency.
pedigree: Named after the Japanese splatter film series.
usFrequency: Never. A genuine Italian underground rarity.

name: Ceremonium
why: Slow and funereal with some genuinely mournful melodies. Into the Autumn Shade is the one to try.
pedigree: A New York band from the first wave of American death-doom, reunited after decades away.
usFrequency: Very rare.

name: Hong Kong Fuck You
why: Tijuana, not Hong Kong, and powerviolence rather than metal — my earlier guess was wrong on both counts. Hëll has described the songs as faster than Hummingbird of Death and shorter than 'You Suffer'. Blink and it's over.
pedigree: Drummer-vocalist Christian Hëll fronts a band with three bassists and no guitarist at all.
usFrequency: Plays constantly in the Southern California and Baja DIY circuit.

name: Brodequin
why: Blastbeat-driven brutality with a real sense of atmosphere for the genre. Still an endurance test.
pedigree: Knoxville band built around medieval torture themes; returned in 2024 after two decades of near-silence.
usFrequency: Rare, but active again.

name: Obscura
paigeNote: Technical death metal. The recent Gothenburg turn is a real plus, but virtuosity-as-appeal holds it mid.
why: Technical death metal that never forgets the melody — fretless bass, harmonised leads, actual choruses. The most Bodom-adjacent musicianship on the bill.
pedigree: Steffen Kummerer's main band; alumni include Christian Münzner, Hannes Grossmann and Linus Klausenitzer, who scattered into Alkaloid, Necrophagist and Blotted Science.
usFrequency: Tours North America fairly regularly.

name: Mizmor
paigeNote: Dissonant blackened doom and drone — chaotic and punishing.
why: Very slow, very heavy, very personal. Rewarding if you give it thirty uninterrupted minutes; punishing if you don't.
pedigree: A.L.N.'s solo project out of Portland, built around losing his faith.
usFrequency: Plays sparingly.
v3Note: Paige put this on her maybe list. My 3 was too low.

name: Cerebral Effusion
why: Slam and gutturals, played well. Nothing here for a melody listener.
pedigree: Long-running Spanish band on the international slam circuit.
usFrequency: Almost never.

name: Temple of Void
why: Heavy and slow but written around real hooks, with occasional clean vocals. A good gateway between the doom and death halves of this festival.
pedigree: Detroit band that's become one of the more reliable names in modern death-doom.
usFrequency: Tours the US periodically.

name: Satan's Revenge on Mankind
why: Twenty-four-track records of pitch-shifted goregrind. Not the blackened speed metal I guessed — it's the filthiest end of the German grind scene, and its defenders call it the best goregrind currently going.
pedigree: Helreath, Tomhet and The Almighty Mr. Goreblast — the East Frisian goregrind underground.
usFrequency: European act; they announced the MDF booking themselves as a rare US trip.

name: Devangelic
why: Down-tuned, blasphemy-themed, relentless. Technically impressive, tonally one-note.
pedigree: Rome-based, a fixture of the European brutal death scene.
usFrequency: Occasional US festival appearances.

name: Cruciamentum
why: Murky, cavernous, dread-heavy death metal that's better composed than most of its peers. Charnel Passages is the record.
pedigree: D.L. leads it; the sound owes a lot to Incantation and early Immolation.
usFrequency: Rare — a few US shows a decade.

name: Rot
why: Thirty-five years of short, filthy, politically angry grind. Historically important in South America, sonically brutal.
pedigree: One of the founding Brazilian grind bands, contemporaries of the early Sepultura scene.
usFrequency: Almost never.

name: One of Nine
why: Already on Paige's list, and for good reason: melodic black metal built entirely around Tolkien, with Summoning-style keys and a theatrical streak reviewers keep comparing to Dimmu Borgir.
pedigree: On Profound Lore; the 2025 album Dawn of the Iron Shadow has a guest turn from Hulder.
usFrequency: Barely plays live at all — this is a rare chance.

name: Goratory
why: Absurdly technical, absurdly juvenile. A weird, beloved corner of American death metal.
pedigree: Massachusetts band, cult status on the strength of Rice on Suede.
usFrequency: Rarely active.

name: Visceral Disgorge
why: Ingesting Putridity is a slam benchmark. Worth knowing they're from here; not worth a set slot over anything else on your list.
pedigree: A hometown band — Baltimore's own, and a fixture of MDF's local contingent.
usFrequency: Local. You can see them in this city any year.

name: Stabbing
why: Texas brutal death that has climbed fast: debut on Comatose Music, then Eon of Obscenity on Century Media in January 2026. Female-fronted gutturals, no melody whatsoever.
pedigree: Frontwoman Bridget Lynch filled in for Suffocation's Ricky Myers on several 2023 shows; drummer Rene Martinez also plays in Flesh Hoarder and Martyred.
usFrequency: Actively touring — they've opened for 200 Stab Wounds.

name: Imperial Crystalline Entombment
paigeNote: Symphonic 'blizzard' black metal — keyboards plus cold wintry atmosphere put it closer to her lane than the speed suggests.
why: Hyper-fast, ice-themed black metal played with silly precision. Fun to see once, and it's a hometown reunion of sorts.
pedigree: Maryland's own — the 'blizzard beats' band, and something of a local legend for Apocalyptic End in White.
usFrequency: Extremely rare; they hardly ever play.
v3Note: Paige put this on her want-to-see list with two stars. My 6 was too low.

name: P.L.F.
why: Fast, short, straightforward grind with no interest in melody whatsoever.
pedigree: Houston grind lifers, closely tied to the Insect Warfare circle also on this bill.
usFrequency: Plays US fests fairly often.

name: Killing Addiction
why: Omega Factor is a genuinely good lost-classic-era Florida death metal EP. A nice obscurity for people who've worn out the famous records.
pedigree: Florida band from the same era and scene as Deicide and Obituary, if never the same profile.
usFrequency: Occasional fest appearances.

name: Immortal Suffering
why: Queens, 1992. Early demos are atypical New York death metal with doomier passages than the Suffocation school. Now on Sevared, with Extreme Torture out in 2023.
pedigree: Ray Lebron joined in 1993 and went on to front Internal Bleeding for years; Dave Zatuchney of Dehumanized joined on guitar in 1994.
usFrequency: Long-dormant cult act — live sets are rare, which makes this a proper reunion booking.

name: Keys to the Astral Gates and Mystic Doors
paigeNote: Genuinely melodic with dungeon-synth keys, but the deliberate lo-fi production is the barrier.
why: My instinct was right that this leans dungeon-synth. Lo-fi black metal with synth passages, drawing on Burzum and demo-era Katatonia. Atmospheric rather than melodic — a maybe for Paige rather than a lock.
pedigree: Pit Dweller and Ludwig the Bloodsucker — pseudonymous, Bandcamp-only, out of Madison, Wisconsin.
usFrequency: Only just started playing live; there's a first-performance tape limited to 50 copies.

name: Fleshless
why: Carcass-derived goregrind, thirty years deep. Consistent, unrelenting, tuneless by design.
pedigree: Long-running Czech band from the same scene that produced Ingrowing, also on this bill.
usFrequency: Almost never.

name: Fake Dust
why: Iron Lung put out their debut LP this year and called it a fully baked maelstrom that only true masters of the craft manage. West Coast grind, played fast and played well.
pedigree: Four-piece from Portland, Oregon, in the Discordance Axis and Insect Warfare lineage — the latter also on this bill.
usFrequency: Tours DIY; there's a dedicated tour promo release.

name: Replicant
why: Gorguts-descended dissonance — angular, unsettling, deliberately anti-melodic. Interesting rather than enjoyable if you want tunes.
pedigree: New Jersey band on Transcending Obscurity; Infinite Mortality got strong reviews.
usFrequency: Tours the East Coast and US fests.

name: Ancient Death
paigeNote: Old-school death metal with no melodic hook.
why: One of the buzz bands of the announcement. Weird, progressive-leaning death metal rather than straight brutality.
pedigree: Their 2025 album landed on a lot of year-end lists, and they hardly ever play shows.
usFrequency: Very rarely — that's part of why they're billed high.

name: Bogside Sniper Squadron
paigeNote: More crust and punk drive than the melodic blackened death I first credited it with.
why: Irish-diaspora death metal with republican themes and a melodic, thrashy streak that reviewers compare to Running Wild-flavoured melodeath. Self-titled LP out on Headsplit in April. More tune here than the poster placement suggests.
pedigree: Deliberately anonymous, reportedly including a member of Philadelphia's Devil Master. Recorded between Pennsylvania and Derry.
usFrequency: Largely a studio project until recently — this may be one of very few live outings.

name: Night of the Vampire
why: Already on Paige's list. Black metal crossed with eighties synths, goth rock and deliberate camp — reviewers file it next to Tribulation and Old Nick.
pedigree: A one-person project run by 'Astral Shadow'; the debut album came out in February 2026.
usFrequency: Barely plays live, so a festival slot is unusual.

name: Coscradh
why: Chaotic, cavernous and genuinely oppressive, with Irish-language titles. Atmosphere over melody.
pedigree: Part of the current Irish underground wave alongside Malthusian.
usFrequency: Very rare US visits.

name: Ingrowing
why: Blast-heavy Eastern European grind with an electronic streak in places. Short and violent.
pedigree: Czech grind veterans, contemporaries of Fleshless.
usFrequency: Almost never.

name: Desolus
paigeNote: Old-school blackened thrash; thrash lineage plus raw production.
why: Confirmed as a hometown-adjacent booking. Satanic sci-fi blackthrash on Hells Headbangers, in the Sodom, Kreator and Absu tradition. Riffy enough to hold attention.
pedigree: A DC power trio; demos were tracked by Sebastian Phillips of Exhumed and Noisem, and mastered by Scott Hull.
usFrequency: Active around the DMV — you can catch them locally.
v3Note: Paige put this on her pass list. My 4 was too high. Her words: “they are from DC tho.”

name: Fire Magic
why: Heroic, battle-themed black metal with classic heavy metal riffing and occasional clean singing. Decibel streamed the album and compared it to early Helheim. A strong dark-horse pick for Paige.
pedigree: Virginia band on Stygian Black Hand; second album Memories of Fire came out in March 2026.
usFrequency: Rare — a small band that doesn't tour much.

name: Crawl
why: Everything Is Noise put it best — they sound exactly like what 'Swedish death metal band' promised in the nineties. Buzzsaw guitar, crust edge, black metal shading. Altar of Disgust is the current record.
pedigree: Kalmar and Stockholm; on Transcending Obscurity. Not the Asarum band of the same name, and nothing to do with the old Entombed EP.
usFrequency: European band; a US festival slot is unusual for them.
v3Note: Paige put this on her maybe list. My 3 was too low.

name: Human Effluence
why: About as far from melody as this bill gets.
pedigree: American brutal death-grind, small-label territory.
usFrequency: Regional.

name: Barren Path
why: Metal Injection summed it up as Gridlink but extra death metal. The debut, Grieving, is twelve songs in about thirteen minutes on Willowtip. Genuinely significant if you follow grind at all.
pedigree: The big one on this list: Takafumi Matsubara and Bryan Fajardo of Gridlink, plus Mauro Cordoba and Rory Kobzina from Gridlink's last album, with Mitchell Luna of Maruta singing. Effectively Gridlink without Jon Chang.
usFrequency: Brand new — MDF is an early marquee appearance.

name: Grave Infestation
why: Deliberately primitive, Autopsy-worshipping death metal. Rotten in a fun way, but no tunes.
pedigree: Vancouver band in the Invictus Productions orbit.
usFrequency: Rare US shows.
v3Note: Paige put this on her maybe list. My 3 was too low.

name: Ruby the Hatchet
why: Seventies-flavoured psych rock with organ and strong clean vocals — the other palate cleanser alongside Lucifer. Barely metal, and that's the appeal on day three.
pedigree: New Jersey band fronted by Jillian Taylor; Tee Pee Records.
usFrequency: Tours the US regularly.

name: Thætas
why: Deliberately disorienting, atonal and short. Cerebral, not catchy.
pedigree: Brooklyn band in the I, Voidhanger / Portal-adjacent corner.
usFrequency: Rare.

name: Mortal Wound
paigeNote: Brutal old-school death.
why: Deliberately primitive caveman death metal in the early Deicide and Cannibal Corpse mould, with war-themed lyrics. The Anus of the World is the 2024 album, name and all.
pedigree: Los Angeles four-piece; releases via Me Saco Un Ojo, Maggot Stomp and now Dark Descent.
usFrequency: Active LA live band.

name: Fermented Mess
why: The name did read goregrind, and it is. Decibel's grind column called them a testament to true grindcore in a sea of filthy pretenders. Internal Rot riffing with Sulfuric Cautery vocals.
pedigree: Long Island trio; drummer connections into Raid and Fear Made Flesh.
usFrequency: DIY shows around New York.

name: Pig's Blood
why: Bestial, war-metal-adjacent death metal. Very heavy, very featureless if you want melody.
pedigree: Portland, Oregon; part of the Nuclear War Now! roster.
usFrequency: Rare.

name: Ripping Remains
why: Portland death-grind, breakneck and old school, with Cannibal Corpse-styled vocals. The Necrodestiny EP came out last October.
pedigree: Risen from Dripping Decay and named after that band's last EP. Drummer Jason Borton has toured or recorded with Jungle Rot, Skeletal Remains and Ripped to Shreds; bassist Michael Freiburger founded Satanik Royalty Records.
usFrequency: Brand new — festival and regional shows so far.

name: Lay Waste
why: Explicitly anti-capitalist and anti-fascist grind. Decibel called it super-pissed tough-guy Nailscore with razor-tight drumming. Deathgrind rather than the brutal death I'd assumed.
pedigree: Harrisonburg, Virginia; played their first show in February 2025. Not the defunct Illinois goregrind band of the same name.
usFrequency: New and building — mostly East Coast so far.
v3Note: Paige put this on her maybe list. My 2 was too low.

name: Raider
paigeNote: Blackened speed thrash — the idiom veto again.
why: Fast, riffy, thrash-leaning and more energetic than most of the death metal here. Worth catching if you're already in the room.
pedigree: Western Canadian band, Alberta scene.
usFrequency: Rare US appearances.
paigeQuote: thrash/death metal band from Waterloo Kitchener Canada
v3Note: Paige put this on her want-to-see list with two stars. My 3 was too low.

name: Crud
why: Not grind at all — this is slow, miserable sludge and death-doom. Decibel reckons they can hang with the darkest sludge practitioners going. New album Human Decency landed in September.
pedigree: Started in Miami as a two-piece of Julie Mejia on bass and Mariel Zayas-Bazan on drums, later adding guitar and vocals; now spread across Seattle, Savannah and Gainesville.
usFrequency: Touring again, with Baltimore-area dates this year.
v3Note: Paige put this on her pass list. My 4 was too high.

name: Lathe
paigeNote: Heavy and atmospheric, but no melodic or Scandinavian signal.
why: Sunn O)))-weight drone crossed with pedal steel and spaghetti-western melody, described by its own scene as heavy prairie rock. Completely out of step with everything around it on the poster, which is the appeal.
pedigree: A Baltimore instrumental trio on Grimoire Records — the most local booking on the bill.
usFrequency: Hometown band. You can see them any time.
v3Note: Paige put this on her pass list. My 4 was too high.

name: Blood Vial
why: Pathology and body-horror themed brutal death. Still the thinnest-documented name on the whole bill, so worth re-checking closer to the fest.
pedigree: Baltimore, on Iron Fortress Records — another hometown slot. Not the Virginia Beach dungeon-synth project of the same name.
usFrequency: New and regional.

name: Blood Star
why: Straight-up eighties-styled heavy metal with a huge clean voice out front — closer to HammerFall and Blind Guardian than anything else on the poster. The odd one out here, and probably a top-five Paige pick.
pedigree: Salt Lake City, on Shadow Kingdom; guitarist Jamison Palmer also plays in Visigoth. Madeline Michelle sings.
usFrequency: Rare outside the western US.

name: Unholy Altar
paigeNote: Sweeping leads and gothic touches emerging, but the core is still raw lo-fi black metal.
why: Raw black metal that has grown more atmospheric and melodic across Veil of Death! Shroud of Nite and this year's A Sullen Dark Sky EP. One reviewer called it some of the rawest, bloodiest black metal of recent years. A real contender for Paige.
pedigree: Philadelphia five-piece — Desecrator, Miserer, Evoked Damnator, Cadaver and Lucifer's Rage. Started out playing Bathory and Mayhem covers.
usFrequency: Active in the US underground and coming off a run of high-profile shows.
v3Note: Paige put this on her want-to-see list with two stars. My 5 was too low.
